description: List the machines this session could work on: the ones the user has added (name, ssh host, whether it is a Slurm cluster, and its state: no link running, or the state of Endeavor's connection to it: connecting, connected, starting, queued, ready or failed), "local" for this computer, which one this session uses now, and the Host names from the user's ~/.ssh/config that are not added yet. Starts no connection and runs no ssh. Call it before add_machine or use_machine when the user names a server.
name: list_machines

description: Add a server or a cluster's login node that the user reaches over ssh, so that notebooks can run there. Connects with the user's own ssh configuration, keys and ssh agent (never a password: Endeavor can't ask for one, and neither should you), installs Endeavor's helper there if it is missing, saves the machine, and reports what it found: node name, home folder, whether Slurm is there, the partitions with their limits, and Julia if it is already known. Waits up to 45 seconds; if the connection is still being made it says so, and calling add_machine again with the same host continues. If it can't connect, nothing is saved and the result says what the user must do (usually `ssh-add` to put a key in the agent, or `ssh <host>` once in a terminal to accept the server's identity). Adding a machine that exists updates it. Add a machine only when the user asks for it.

host.description: An ssh alias from ~/.ssh/config, or user@host, optionally with :port.

julia.description: Where Julia is on the machine, if Endeavor should not look for it itself: a path to the julia program, or a shell line that puts it on the PATH, such as `module load julia`. The line runs on the machine as given.

name.description: The name to use for the machine in these tools. Letters, digits, - _ and . only. Defaults to the host.

name: add_machine

description: Put this session's notebooks on a machine: "local" is this computer, any other value is a machine's name from list_machines. Connects, then attaches to the Julia runtime already running there, starts one, or on a Slurm cluster submits a job for it. Returns within 45 seconds with the state. ready: the result has browser_url (the link to give the user), the node, and whether a runtime was already running there. starting or queued: the runtime is not up yet; the result has the job's id and the queue's state and reason, and pluto_session_status shows progress. On a cluster with no job running and no resources given, nothing is submitted: the result has needs_job true and the machine's default resources, and you ask the user to confirm them (or choose others) and call use_machine again with them. The resources you give are saved as the machine's defaults. The session starts with no notebook on the new machine (a session's notebook stays on the machine it was made on); the project remembers the machine and folder for later sessions. Switch machines, and submit jobs, only when the user asks. From here on list_folder, read_file and run_shell run on that machine, and notebook paths are that machine's.

account.description: Cluster only: the Slurm account to charge. Saved as the machine's default.

cpus.description: Cluster only: CPUs for the job.

extra_sbatch_flags.description: Cluster only: more flags for sbatch, each as one string such as "--constraint=a100". They run as given.

folder.description: The session's folder on the machine: where new notebooks go and relative paths start. Defaults to the machine's home folder.

gpus.description: Cluster only: GPUs for the job, as a count, or a Slurm gres string such as "gpu:a100:2".

hours.description: Cluster only: the job's time limit in hours (a fraction is fine). The job, and the notebooks in it, end then.

machine.description: "local" for this computer, or a machine's name from list_machines.

memory_gb.description: Cluster only: memory for the job in GB.

partition.description: Cluster only: the Slurm partition. Defaults to the machine's saved default, else the cluster's.

name: use_machine

description: Stop the Julia runtime on a machine ("local" is this computer) for every client that uses it, and on a cluster cancel its job. It ends all the notebooks running there, the user's too, and anyone else's. First it checks for other sessions that were active in a notebook in the last 15 minutes; if there is one and force is not true, it stops nothing and the result names who (the client's label, how long ago, which notebook): tell the user, and call again with force true only if they agree. Stop the runtime only when the user asks, such as to give a cluster node back. This session stays pointed at the machine: a later notebook call says it was stopped, and use_machine starts it again.

force.description: Stop even though another session was active lately. Only after the user agreed.

machine.description: "local" for this computer, or a machine's name from list_machines.

name: stop_machine
